title: Password Strength Segments
statement:
A password consists of lowercase English letters only. A string is **valid** if it contains at least one vowel (`a`, `e`, `i`, `o`, `u`) and at least one consonant (every other letter).

The **strength** of a password is the maximum number of contiguous subsegments the whole password can be divided into such that every subsegment is valid. The subsegments must be consecutive, non-empty, non-overlapping and together cover the entire password. If the password itself is not valid, its strength is `0`.

Given a password, print its strength.
inputFormat: A single line containing the password string.
outputFormat: Print a single integer: the strength of the password.
constraints: password consists of lowercase English letters only

examples.explanation: The password can be divided into `hack`, `er` and `rank`; each contains a vowel and a consonant. It cannot be divided into more than 3 valid subsegments.
The password has no consonant, so it is not valid and its strength is 0.
`bca` and `eb` are both valid. Cutting earlier is impossible: `bc` has no vowel.

hints: A segment becomes valid the moment it has seen both a vowel and a consonant. Is there any reason to extend it past that point?
Scan from the left; whenever the current segment has both kinds of letters, close it and start a new one. Closing as early as possible leaves the most characters for later segments.
Characters left over at the end (an incomplete segment) can simply be merged into the last closed segment. If no segment was ever closed, the answer is 0.
